text:
maria: Quick heads-up: tomorrow we flip the backup-uploader RBAC split (uploader-reader + uploader-writer). Before we do we need to resolve KMS grant fallout and a tempfile vuln found in the legacy backup-agent.
aj: noted. if we change the role principal, existing KMS grants will no longer map. we need a grant migration strategy (not just renaming).
maria: agree. also found staging is still accepting objects without SSE headers (SSE-C/SSE-KMS missing) during a canary run. that's risky for compliance.
sam: i'm running an audit to enumerate objects missing server-side encryption in prod backups bucket. quick plan: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket prod-backups --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,LastModified:LastModified}' --max-items 1000` then `aws s3api head-object` per key to check `SSECustomerAlgorithm`/`ServerSideEncryption`.
claire: vuln scan flagged the agent writing `.dump.tmp` with 0644 perms in /var/tmp before upload. if upload fails the file can be read by other users on the node. risk blowup for multi-tenant hosts.
devansh: that has to be hotpatched: create secure temp with 0600 + O_EXCL and atomic rename to final name, and ensure cleanup on failure. also we should crash the upload with non-zero on permission mismatch so CI picks it up.
maria: propose short-term mitigations: 1) push agent patch to master and run a canary image, 2) add S3 bucket policy to deny PutObject without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` or `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms` for uploads from uploader-writer principal, 3) create a scoped KMS grant migration flow.
aj: sample deny policy I tested in a sandbox: `{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/uploader-writer"},"Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::prod-backups/*","Condition":{"Null":{"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption":true}}}`. We'll scope to the role to avoid blocking other services.
sam: scan results so far: ~9 objects without SSE in last 30 days, many from dev snapshots. i'll open a remediation ticket with list and owners. for objects already uploaded without SSE we can use `aws s3 cp` + `--server-side-encryption aws:kms` to reupload, or `aws s3api copy-object --copy-source bucket/key --bucket bucket --key key --server-side-encryption aws:kms` if allowed. note: copy preserves object content but requires read access.
claire: branch `secure-tempfile-agent` created. PR includes test that creates a temp file and asserts mode == 0600; failing check blocks merge. also added a systemd tmpfile unit suggestion for dedicated fleets.
devansh: KMS migration approach: for each CMK used by backup pipeline create a short-lived grant for the new role (`GrantTokens` optional) and update restore workers to request grant_id from encops service before attempting decrypt. after a validation window revoke the old grants. script will log `grantId` and timestamp to secrets manager.
aj: also enable CloudTrail filter rule to alert on `PutObject` without SSE and on `CreateGrant`/`RetireGrant` so we can detect unexpected grants. I'll add a logmetric for `S3WithoutSSE` and a pager.
sam: caution: do NOT revoke old grants en masse until we've confirmed all restore jobs can use the new grant flow. add a staged revoke: revoke for non-active projects first, then escalate.
encops-bot: NOTICE: canary job `uploader-canary-7` had AccessDenied when requesting KMS decrypt (service account still referencing old role).
maria: holding the prod flip until the canary is fixed. timeline: claire -> complete agent PR + push canary (ETA 1.5h), aj -> deploy S3 deny policy to prod (ETA 45m), sam -> finish audit and remediation ticket (ETA 2h), devansh -> publish grant migration script & test (ETA 3h).
claire: PR includes a temporary runtime check: if tempfile created with perms >0600 agent logs error and aborts upload; will remove after rollout. added unit/integration tests.
maria: after patch + S3 policy we should run a controlled re-encryption of one affected snapshot and run a restore smoke test to confirm the new grant flow works end-to-end. create a checklist item in SEC-2029.
devansh: i'll add the automation: `create-grant -> store-grantid(secret-store) -> rotate-job-to-use-grantid -> monitor decrypt-errors -> revoke-old-grant`. also add a canary that attempts decrypt with revoked grant to verify revocation effective.
encops-bot: TICKET: SEC-2029 created for unencrypted uploads + grant migration; assigned to @sam and @devansh.
deploy-bot: pipeline queued: `backup-agent:secure-tempfile` canary image -> requires manual approve to run.
maria: thanks team. keep updates here with any failed restores or unexpected AccessDenied events. We'll capture this for the compliance audit note after resolution. :white_check_mark:
